brief_course_description: This course provides students with deep understanding of object-oriented programming concepts. Topics covered include classes, objects, instantiation, methods, and instance variables, I/O, encapsulation, static fields and static methods, overloading, constructors, scope of declarations, overriding, composition, Java API packages, inheritance, garbage collection, polymorphism, final methods and final classes, abstract classes and methods, interfaces, and introduction to GUI.
CLO5: Develop Graphical User Interfaces in Java.
weekly_topics: W1: OOP basics; classes & objects; instantiation | W2: methods & instance variables; I/O | W3: encapsulation; static fields & methods | W4: overloading; Quiz 1 | W5: constructors | W6: scope; overriding; GUI I/O (JOptionPane) | W7: composition; Assignment 1 (encapsulation & composition) | W8: Midterm Exam | W9: Java API packages; inheritance | W10: inheritance | W11: GUI intro; Swing components; text/images; text fields; Quiz 2 | W12: polymorphism; abstract classes & methods | W13: abstract classes & methods; final classes & methods | W14: interfaces; event handling intro | W15: common event types & listener interfaces; anonymous inner class for event handling | W16: Final Exam
lab_schedule: Two-hour weekly lab sessions covering the week by week topics mentioned above.
teaching_methods: General lectures using electronic tools; Critical Thinking; Written Assignments; Laboratory Based Learning
textbook_1_title: Java How to Program, Early Objects
reference_1_title: JAVA from the ground up: The Easy Guide For Beginners
other_resources: jGRASP v 2.0.4_01 software: lightweight IDE providing automatic software visualizations; developed by Auburn University (Samuel Ginn College of Engineering).
learning_strategies: Active learning strategies to encourage participation and group discussion; guidance to understand problem nature and analysis; assignments individually and in teams.
attendance_policy: Warnings/penalties: 1st warning at 10% absence of class hours; 2nd warning at 20%; failing grade at 25%. Exception to failing grade may be made for serious illness or death of immediate family member with dean approval; in such case student receives W grade.
plagiarism_policy: Using someone else's idea/words/projects/artwork/phrasing/sentence structure/other work without proper acknowledgement; dishonest misrepresentation; suspected students investigated; guilty students face disciplinary action per university rules.
